extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers / Royal Society members; practitioners and readers of 17th-century experimental natural philosophy
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting observational and experimental natural-history or physical experiments: describe apparatus, methods, observations, and inferences so other natural philosophers can evaluate and reproduce the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground reports in observations and experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘a specimen of natural philosophy improved and advanced by observations and experiments’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favour empiricism over mere speculation — explain phenomena from experimental observation and report notable experiments carried out in diverse places. Emphasise experiments as the basis for claims about qualities and powers of bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide demonstrations, not mere assertions
rubrics_metrics.description: Author ‘undertakes to demonstrate all those he advances’ rather than merely proposing rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposing laws or rules (e.g., laws of motion), supply proofs, demonstrations, or detailed argumentation rather than unsupported statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with and reference prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘is not ignorant of what has been lately published by some famous mathematicians…’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Situate new claims in the context of existing literature; acknowledge relevant recent publications and explain agreements or differences with them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe apparatus and measurements precisely
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a crystal globe with specified diameter and a graduated neck; use of a 20-foot telescope and timing of eclipses to minutes/seconds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report exact instrument specifications (sizes, graduations), observational setups (e.g., telescope focal length), and measurement units so others can reproduce observations and assess precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide step-by-step procedural detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed account of filling the globe, immersion in ice and salt, observing rises/descents in the neck, taking the globe out at specific marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the sequence of actions, initial conditions, and how observations were made (when and how the apparatus was manipulated) to allow replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control initial conditions and ensure reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Noting that when ‘care were taken to put it to the very same degree… the whole vessel might be considered as a very nice thermometer’ and that repeating produced similar orders of alteration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeat experiments under consistent starting conditions; document how initial state was set and show that repeated trials yield comparable behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report anomalies, instrument failures, and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Account of the globe bursting, inability to see frost veins, and failing to hit the 'nick' to observe intermediate veins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document unexpected events, apparatus breakage, negative results, and observational limits; these inform interpretation and future replication attempts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record precise times and compare to established tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Eclipse timings given to hours, minutes, seconds and comparison 'According to Riccioli's tables' and 'According to the Rudolphin tables.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide exact timing/chronological data and compare observational results against standard tables or predictions to validate observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include illustrations and figures to support descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference to PL 13 figures showing leaf pieces, cartridge, and theca (‘PL 13, fig. 2… fig. 5 shows the cartridge itself; and fig. 6 the theca’).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply plates/figures and label them to clarify morphological descriptions and experimental set-ups; visual evidence strengthens the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give detailed morphological and taxonomic descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguishing the bee species by forcipes size, hairiness, tongue shape; citation of Mr. Kirby's Monographia Apum and species name Apis Willughbiella.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide diagnostic anatomical traits, comparisons to known species, and taxonomic attribution (including authorities) to support identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide sensory and material descriptions of samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of the 'pap or batter' consistency, colour ‘between syrup of violets and conserve of red roses’, acid taste, unpleasant smell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record texture, colour, taste/smell (where appropriate), and state of preservation of sample material as part of natural-history reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use corroboration from independent observers
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple letters and observers (Mr. Ray, Mr. Snell, Mr. Jessop) confirm leaf-bitten evidence and locations where cartridges found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corroborate findings via independent collectors/observers and report their agreements or disagreements to strengthen claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derive causal inferences from multiple parallel instances
rubrics_metrics.description: From many parallel instances one may answer whether the maggot, not the old bee, covers cells: 'From what has been observed concerning this bee, and by a great many more parallel instances, we may answer the question… that it is the maggot and not the old one.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base causal or functional claims on repeated analogous observations rather than single anecdotes; present the pattern of evidence leading to the inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid premature conclusions; seek mechanical or natural explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: On spiders: initial puzzlement thinking they could fly, then describing mechanical way threads are projected and fastened by 'beating their tails' to explain observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not jump to extraordinary explanations; examine mechanical/natural mechanisms and describe careful observation that can resolve apparent paradoxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess and critique theoretical claims against empirical facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers note the falsity of Cartesian principles in the Elementa Physica review and assert that propositions should be proven rather than presumed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating theoretical works, check internal consistency with observed facts, point out mistaken hypotheses, and demand empirical proof or demonstration.
